<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The `.SRCINFO` file defines metadata for the `tuicode-bin` package, including source URLs, checksums, and dependencies. The package is sourced from the official GitHub repository (https://github.com/LucasionGS/tuicode) and points to release binaries for both x86_64 and aarch64 architectures. The `sha256sums` are provided for both architectures and match the respective binary packages, ensuring integrity of the prebuilt tarballs.

The source URLs use the `::` syntax to rename the downloaded files locally, which is standard practice in AUR packaging to avoid naming conflicts. The package does not use `SKIP` for checksums, and the sources are from the project's official release page, which is expected for a binary package. There are no signs of obfuscated URLs, unexpected network locations, or scripts that could introduce malicious behavior.

No build-time scripts or commands are visible in this file, as `.SRCINFO` is a metadata-only file generated from the PKGBUILD. The package provides standard optdepends for optional features (clipboard tools, language servers, debuggers), all of which are legitimate and contextually appropriate for a terminal-based code editor.
</details>

</summary>

LLM auditresponse for PKGBUILD:
<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD retrieves a prebuilt binary package from the project's official GitHub release page and extracts its contents into the package directory. The source URLs point directly to the declared upstream (`https://github.com/LucasionGS/tuicode`), which is expected and appropriate. Checksums are provided for both architectures and are not set to 'SKIP', indicating verified integrity.

The `package()` function performs a straightforward copy of the extracted `/usr` directory into `$pkgdir`, which is standard behavior for binary packages. There are no signs of obfuscated code, unauthorized network requests, or suspicious system modifications. All dependencies and optional dependencies are clearly stated and relevant to the application's functionality.

The package follows common AUR packaging practices for a `-bin` package. While it distributes a precompiled binary (which inherently limits auditability of the upstream code), the PKGBUILD itself contains no malicious logic or supply-chain risks.
</details>
